findings.reason: the node needs a case with exit 1 and no added failure id (or an empty `failure_ids`), otherwise the section's own separate guarantee is untested and a half-implemented check passes its gate.
findings.text: §39 declares one refusing arm as "`after_suite` records a non-zero exit or any failure id not present in `baseline_suite`" and separately guarantees "It never records gate `passed` for a run whose own `after_suite` exit is non-zero", but its first case sets exit 1 *and* an added failure id together, so a lander that compares failure ids only (ignoring the exit) passes every case and the negative control while still promoting a non-zero-exit run whose failures are all present in `baseline_suite` — the ordinary red-main shape

findings.reason: the section's stated mechanism cannot produce its own done-when; it must name `_unreadable_figure_review_records` (or say the lander distinguishes the two the way promotion does) or case 2 will be implemented against a reader that erases the distinction.
findings.text: §40 requires "An unparsable figure record is recorded as unreadable, not absent" but its deliverable names only two mechanisms, reading through `promotion_checks._newest_figure_review` and judging completeness by the blocking-finding predicate; `_newest_figure_review` (promotion_checks.py:552) swallows `(OSError, ValueError)` and returns `None` for an unparsable record exactly as for a run with no figure review, and its own docstring says the caller must ask `_unreadable_figure_review_records` which of the two it holds — a function the section never names, so a worker implementing the deliverable as written records case 2's record as absent and cannot pass the case
